verdicts.title: adaclip is priced with train_batch_size under sampling_mode='k_out_of_t', whose expected batch size is dataset_size*k/t
verdicts.reasoning: Every link verified in the current tree. _dp_trainer.py:1472 sets expected_batch_size = a.train_batch_size; _build_mechanism (:4470-4479) wraps the base Gaussian in dpsgd_acc.adaclip(..., expected_batch_size=expected_batch_size) BEFORE the `if a.sampling_mode == 'k_out_of_t'` branch at :4495, so the adaclip sigma_b = train_batch_size * 0.05 regardless of sampler. The k_out_of_t runtime sampler is built at _dpftrl.py:332 with t=n_steps, and KOutOfTSampler.expected_batch_size (packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_k_out_of_t.py:110-112) is num_samples*k/t. _steps_breakdown (_dp_trainer.py:4740-4767) makes n_steps = max_steps when set, else ceil(num_train_epochs*ceil(dataset_size/train_batch_size)); so dataset_size*k/t equals train_batch_size only when k == num_train_epochs (and never reliably when max_steps is set). _adaptive.py:106-121 and :580-600 confirm the runtime noises the realised rate num_clipped/batch_size with std fraction_noise_std, i.e. absolute count noise = realised_batch * 0.05, so the actual noise is SMALLER than accounted when k < epochs -> epsilon is understated. Reachability verified by execution: TrainingArguments(per_device_train_batch_size=32, num_train_epochs=3, privacy_target_epsilon=3.0, clipping_mode='adaptive', sampling_mode='k_out_of_t', sampling_kwargs={'k':1,'allocation':'block'}) is accepted with clipping_mode still 'adaptive' and zero warnings; _training_arguments.py:1281-1292 resolves adaptive->fixed only for DP-FTRL mechanisms, and :1311-1345 validates only presence of k/allocation and the allocation literal. No test pins the correct behaviour: the only trainer k_out_of_t guarantee test (packages/opaque-transformers/tests/validation/test_dp_guarantees.py:237-259) uses the default clipping_mode='fixed'. Severity held at medium rather than raised: clipping_mode defaults to 'fixed' and sampling_mode defaults to poisson, so two explicit opt-ins plus a k that disagrees with the horizon are needed; but when they are set the understatement is silent and ~3x. Not a duplicate of an open tracked issue: Bazalt #767 (the DP-SGD sampling/adaptive-clipping umbrella) has all children closed and is a parent, not a filed duplicate.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: With clipping_mode='adaptive' and sampling_mode='k_out_of_t' the accountant is handed expected_batch_size = train_batch_size while the sampler draws batches averaging dataset_size*k/n_steps. Reproduced end to end with the real factories: dataset_size=10000, per_device_train_batch_size=32, num_train_epochs=3 -> steps_per_epoch=313, n_steps=939, so the sampler's expected batch is 10000*1/939 = 10.65, not 32. k_out_of_t(adaclip(gaussian(1.0), expected_batch_size=32), k=1, t=939, allocation='block').epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.16464 (effective_noise_multiplier 0.954480), whereas the same process built with the sampler's true expectation 10.65 gives 0.49026 (effective_noise_multiplier 0.728991) - a 3.0x understatement of the reported epsilon, in the unsafe direction. The mismatch is unbounded when max_steps is set explicitly, because _steps_breakdown then uses t = max_steps with no link to train_batch_size at all. TrainingArguments accepts the configuration with no warning (verified by execution). The direction reverses (conservative) when k > num_train_epochs.

verdicts.title: the #881 random-allocation memoisation never serves a hit because epsilon_at folds a Monte-Carlo-only field into its cache key
verdicts.reasoning: The substantive claim reproduces. epoch_pld (packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_random_allocation_cache.py:29-46) is an lru_cache keyed on the whole frozen DiscretizationConfig, which includes mc_resolution and mc_failure_probability (discretization.py:17-40, frozen dataclass -> those fields are in __eq__/__hash__). DpProcess.epsilon_at (_base.py:212-227) recomputes mc_resolution = min(configured, delta/2.0) and passes it down, while delta_at does not, so each distinct delta yields a distinct config and therefore a distinct epoch_pld key. The Rust transform is delta- and MC-independent: random_allocation.rs:164-227 plus Accuracy::derive/alloc_remove/alloc_add read only discretization, log_mass_truncation_bound, max_conv_grid, max_grid_size and tail_mass_truncation - no mc_* field is touched. The per-process pld_cache (_pld_cache.py) keys on the same config object, so it misses in lockstep. Measured (k=8, t=512, default discretization, prebuilt native ext): eps(1e-5) 16.52s misses=1; eps(1e-5) repeat 0.01s; eps(1e-6) 16.64s misses=2 hits=0; delta_at(3.0) 16.54s misses=3 hits=0. So a delta sweep re-pays the full O(G^2) transform for a result that cannot depend on delta. TWO CORRECTIONS to the finding as written: (a) the title's 'never serves a hit' is false - I observed hits=1 when a structurally different process (allocation='total' at the same nm/k/t) queried the same delta, so epoch_pld does deduplicate across distinct processes at a fixed delta; its only useless dimension is delta; (b) the reported delta_at(3.0) value of 6.67e-09 did not reproduce - I measured 0.0 at that configuration (immaterial to the defect). No privacy impact; pure wasted work. Not a duplicate of open #911, which is about Monte Carlo calibration cost, not this deterministic transform.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Any epsilon-vs-delta sweep, or simply epsilon_at(1e-5) followed by epsilon_at(1e-6) or delta_at(eps), on a k-out-of-t or balls-in-bins/identity process recomputes the delta-independent O(G^2) random-allocation transform from scratch, because epsilon_at rewrites mc_resolution to delta/2 and that field is part of the epoch_pld cache key. Measured at k=8, t=512 with default discretization: 16.5s, then 0.01s for the identical repeat, then 16.6s for eps(1e-6) and 16.5s for delta_at(3.0), with epoch_pld.cache_info() showing hits=0 misses=3. The cache is not entirely dead - a different process (allocation='total') at the same delta did hit it - but every change of delta wastes a full transform. Efficiency only; the returned epsilon values are correct.

verdicts.title: AdaClip.__post_init__ guards only the non-positive half of its range, so expected_batch_size=inf still prices the quantile release as free
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced exactly through the real serialization codec. packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/mechanisms/_adaclip.py:40-62 validates only `fraction_noise_std <= 0`, `expected_batch_size <= 0` and `num_groups < 1 or != int(...)`, none of which is true for +inf, and the comment at :40-44 states the validation exists precisely so deserialization 'cannot produce an instance that prices the quantile release as free'. Executed: state_dict(adaclip(gaussian(1.1), expected_batch_size=250.0, num_groups=4)) -> field replaced with float('inf') -> from_state_dict(template, sd) ACCEPTED; effective_noise_multiplier = 1.1 (the bare inner multiplier) instead of 1.0957654, and poisson(rebuilt, 0.01).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.1422977567766371, bit-identical to poisson(gaussian(1.1), 0.01).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.1422977567766371, versus 0.14418327866598055 for the untampered process. Same result for fraction_noise_std=inf. NaN in either field is accepted by __post_init__ too but fails closed downstream (ValueError 'Infinite epsilon bounds: [NaN, NaN]'), so +inf is the surviving fail-open value, as claimed. The secondary claim also reproduces: AdaClip(inner=poisson(gaussian(1.1), 0.01), ...) constructs without error and effective_noise_multiplier returns None from a `-> float` property, because __post_init__ does not validate `inner` while the adaclip() factory does (:164-173). Severity held at low, not medium: this is not reachable at defaults or through any supported API - the adaclip() factory and normal serialization round-trips never produce inf, so it needs a corrupted or hand-edited accountant checkpoint. It is a fail-open hardening gap in exactly the threat model the code comments claim to cover, not a live epsilon bug. Bazalt #764 ('make accounting state fail closed across serialization') is an all-children-closed umbrella, i.e. the parent this would be filed under, not a duplicate.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A hand-edited or corrupted accountant checkpoint whose AdaClip JSON carries Infinity for expected_batch_size (or fraction_noise_std) is rebuilt by from_state_dict without error; sigma_b becomes infinite, the K/(4*sigma_b^2) term in adaclip_sensitivity vanishes, and the adaptive-clipping quantile releases are priced at zero. Verified through the real codec: effective_noise_multiplier collapses from 1.0957654 to 1.1 and poisson(...,0.01).epsilon_at(1e-5) drops from 0.14418328 to 0.14229776, which is bit-identical to the unamplified-quantile poisson(gaussian(1.1),0.01) figure. NaN fails closed with a ValueError downstream, so +inf is the only fail-open value. Separately, AdaClip constructed directly with a non-Gaussian/non-NonPrivate inner (e.g. a Poisson process) is accepted by __post_init__ and its effective_noise_multiplier property returns None despite a `-> float` annotation. Neither is reachable through the adaclip() factory or an untampered checkpoint.

verdicts.title: docs still name the removed random_allocation accounting factory
verdicts.reasoning: Verified directly. docs/user-guide/accounting.md:586 reads '... Balls-in-Bins with `identity_strategy()`, and `random_allocation` and `k_out_of_t`, use deterministic transforms.' The two neighbouring backticked names in the same sentence (identity_strategy(), k_out_of_t) are real public API, so `random_allocation` reads as one too. It is not: `opaque.dpsgd.accounting.__all__` executes to ['adaclip','gaussian','k_out_of_t','parallel_poisson','poisson'] (run in the repo venv), and a repo-wide grep for random_allocation outside .git/.venv returns only this docs line plus legitimately-surviving internal names (_random_allocation_cache.py, the Rust random_allocation_gaussian_pld and its PyO3 binding, and the third-party `random_allocation` cross-validation package imported in packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/accounting/test_cross_validation_allocation.py). It is the only user-facing reference. Severity low and already at the floor: the consequence is an AttributeError for a reader who copies the name, i.e. loud, not silently wrong. No open tracked issue covers it - #845 is the citation-verification sweep, a different defect class.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A reader of the Monte-Carlo-vs-deterministic note in docs/user-guide/accounting.md:586 writes dpsgd_acc.random_allocation(...) and gets an AttributeError, because that factory was folded into k_out_of_t(..., allocation='block') and opaque.dpsgd.accounting now exports only adaclip, gaussian, k_out_of_t, parallel_poisson and poisson. Documentation-only; no runtime or accounting consequence, and the failure is loud.
